comments.content: `valueFromLine` builds a `std::string_view` of length `digits` but then calls `std::strtol`/`std::strtof` with `sub.data()`. `strtol`/`strtof` do not respect the string_view length; they parse until a non-numeric char or the NUL terminator. For any field that is not the last one on the line (e.g. the coordinate/component fields parsed in a loop), this will read past `digits` into the adjacent field and produce wrong values whenever fields are packed without a separating blank (fixed-width FRD format). You need to copy the `digits` characters into a NUL-terminated buffer (e.g. `std::string(sub)`) before calling strtol/strtof, or pass an explicit end pointer via `std::from_chars` for integers.

In the `code1` branch, if `mapNodes.at(node)` throws `std::out_of_range`, it is caught and only a warning is logged, but `countNodes` is still incremented and execution continues. Afterwards the block `if ((vecValues.size() + scaValues.size()) == numComps)` calls `vecArray->SetTuple(mapNodes.at(node), ...)` and `scaArrays[...]->SetTuple1(mapNodes.at(node), ...)` with the same invalid `node`, which will throw again — this time uncaught — aborting the whole conversion. Guard the SetTuple calls so they are skipped for nodes not present in `mapNodes`.

In `readNodes`, `coords` is filled only when the line starts with `keyCodeCoord` (" -1"). If a line inside the node block does not match (e.g. a stray/blank line), `coords` stays empty and `points->SetPoint(nodeID, coords.data())` is called with a null/empty pointer, causing out-of-bounds reads. Only call `SetPoint`/increment when a valid coordinate line was parsed.
